study type: Secondary analysis of a clinical trial
cohort: The cohort consisted of 931 women whose fetuses were in breech presentation between 34 and 36 weeks' gestation and were cephalic at birth.
finding: Women whose fetuses achieved a cephalic presentation at birth via successful ECV were not at greater risk of obstetrical interventions at birth compared to those whose fetuses spontaneously turned to cephalic presentation.
mod_finding: No differences were found in the incidence of Cesarean section, instrumental birth, or normal vaginal birth after successful ECV compared with SCV, though multiparous women with successful ECV were half as likely to require a Cesarean section.
gest_age: 34-36 weeks at the time of breech presentation assessment
